post_title: How many UN member states will vote in favour of the annual TPNW resolution at the First Committee's 2026 action phase?

question.title: How many UN member states will vote in favour of the annual TPNW resolution at the First Committee's 2026 action phase?
question.description:
The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW), adopted in 2017 and entered into force on 22 January 2021, is the first legally binding international agreement to comprehensively prohibit nuclear weapons. As of July 2026, 70 states had ratified and 95 had signed the treaty. Every year, the UN General Assembly's First Committee (Disarmament and International Security) considers a draft resolution — historically designated L.6 and titled "Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons" — that welcomes the treaty and calls on states to sign and ratify it.

The resolution is adopted each year by a recorded vote, opposed by the nuclear-weapon states and most NATO/umbrella states. The number of states voting in favour grew over time as ratifications increased: the First Committee vote was 123 in favour on the 2016 mandate resolution, 118 in favour in 2020, and 144 in favour (3 against, 30 abstentions) in 2024. Growth has slowed because the pool of likely supporters (mostly the Global South — Africa, Latin America, the Pacific, and parts of Asia) has largely been tapped, while European and nuclear-umbrella states remain opposed or abstaining. Year-to-year counts can shift by a handful of states due to new ratifications, absences, or shifts in a government's position.

The First Committee's 81st session runs 5 October to 6 November 2026 in New York, with action on all draft resolutions scheduled for 27 October to 3 November 2026. The nuclear-weapons cluster, which includes the TPNW resolution, is typically among the first clusters voted during the action phase; in recent years that vote has fallen in late October or the first days of November. Official vote records are published in UN Meetings Coverage summaries and compiled by civil-society monitors ICAN and Reaching Critical Will.

question.resolution_criteria: This question asks how many UN member states cast a "Yes" vote on the recorded vote for the annual draft resolution on the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW) — the text historically numbered L.6 and titled "Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons" — taken by the First Committee (Disarmament and International Security) of the UN General Assembly during the 81st session's action-on-drafts period (27 October to 3 November 2026). Resolution reads the officially recorded First Committee vote tally for this resolution as it stands on or after 29 October 2026, taking the number in the "In favour" field as reported in the UN Meetings Coverage summary of the relevant First Committee meeting ([press.un.org/en/first-committee](https://press.un.org/en/first-committee)) or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) such as ICAN or Reaching Critical Will reporting the official First Committee tally. For example, if 144 states vote in favour, this resolves as 144.
question.fine_print: Only the First Committee recorded vote on the full/main TPNW draft resolution counts — not votes on individual operative or preambular paragraphs, and not the separate General Assembly plenary adoption that occurs in December 2026. If the resolution is adopted without a recorded vote, or if no such resolution is put to a recorded vote during the 81st session, the question is annulled. If the primary source does not report the count, the figure from credible sources reporting the official First Committee tally will be used.
